title: Depreciation methods
examples: Which method results in a lower residual value?
How does the method choice affect tax calculations?
Can you show the calculation for the first year's depreciation?

explain.say: Today we look at how assets lose value over time. This process is called depreciation. We will compare two common methods.

The straight-line method spreads the cost evenly each year. You calculate a fixed amount to subtract every single year. For example, if something costs one hundred dollars and lasts ten years, you subtract ten dollars each year.

The reducing balance method uses a percentage of the remaining value. This means the amount you subtract gets smaller each year. Imagine a car losing value faster when it is new. This method reflects that idea.

items: Uses a percentage of remaining value

explain.say: Let us try an example. Suppose a machine costs five thousand dollars and has a useful life of five years. Using straight-line, the annual depreciation is one thousand dollars. The value after four years is one thousand dollar times four years, subtracted from five thousand dollars.

Now for the reducing balance method on the same machine. If we use a ten percent rate, the first year's loss is five hundred dollars. The value after four years will be calculated by applying ten percent reduction four times consecutively.

faq.q: What is the difference between the two methods?
faq.a: The straight-line method loses value evenly each year. The reducing balance method loses value based on the asset's current book value.
asks: Are they both ways to depreciate?
Which one is better for accounting?

faq.q: Does the method choice affect the final value?
faq.a: Yes, they almost always result in different residual values. The straight-line method usually results in a higher final value than reducing balance.
asks: Will the final values be the same?
Does the method change the total depreciation?

faq.q: Do I need to know the residual value beforehand?
faq.a: For straight-line, you often use a residual value, but for reducing balance, you just need the initial cost and the percentage rate.
asks: Is residual value needed for RB?
What if I don't know the scrap value?

faq.q: Which method is more realistic for electronics?
faq.a: Reducing balance is often considered more realistic for electronics. New technology tends to lose value faster initially.

faq.q: Can I mix and match the methods?
faq.a: Generally, you must stick to one method for consistency in your accounting records. Do not switch methods mid-calculation.

facts: Depreciation is the accounting process of allocating the cost of a tangible asset over its useful life.
Straight-line depreciation calculates an equal amount of expense each accounting period.
Reducing balance depreciation calculates depreciation based on the asset's declining book value.
The initial cost of an asset is the starting point for both calculations.

quiz.say: A machine costs $10,000 and is depreciated using straight-line over 5 years. What is the book value after 4 years?
quiz.why: The annual straight-line depreciation is two thousand dollars. Subtracting this from the initial cost gives the correct value.

wrong.1: This is the value after 2 years, forgetting to calculate the full four years of depreciation.
wrong.2: This assumes the asset has no residual value and is fully depreciated after four years.
wrong.3: This incorrectly assumes that no depreciation has occurred over the four-year period.

quiz.say: A vehicle costs $30,000 and is depreciated using a reducing balance method at 15 percent per year. What is the book value after 2 years?
quiz.why: First year loss is four thousand five hundred dollars. Second year loss is based on the reduced value, resulting in the correct final amount.

wrong.1: This calculates the loss as a flat fifteen percent of the original cost each year.
wrong.2: This incorrectly calculates the loss by adding the two year percentages together.
wrong.3: This incorrectly calculates the loss by subtracting the percentage from the original cost.

quiz.say: If an asset costs $20,000 and is depreciated using straight-line over 4 years with no residual value, what is the depreciation charge in year 3?
quiz.show: SL: $20k, 4 yrs, no residual. Year 3 charge?
quiz.why: Straight-line depreciation means the charge is the same every year. Divide twenty thousand by four years for the correct annual amount.

wrong.0: This is what you get if you divide the cost by five years instead of four years.
wrong.1: This is half the original cost, which is not the required annual charge.
wrong.2: This incorrectly assumes that the asset is fully written off by the end of year two.
